guide: Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: targets for margin, utilisation, callbacks, close rate, reviews and cash cover, and the red and amber days for renewals.
Check Lead Sources and Technicians. They hold the sources, what each costs a month and the six lead technicians the review sheets use.
Enter each month of each source on Marketing Spend: spend, calls, booked jobs, sold jobs and revenue. Cost per lead, cost per booked job and revenue per spend fill in by themselves.
Read Source Results: each source for 3 months, 12 months and the 12 before, with a keep, renegotiate or drop verdict from the limits in Settings.
Enter recent jobs on Jobs with source, price, margin and whether a review was asked for and received. Enter Reviews and Referrals counts for each technician and month.
List every licence, insurance, registration, inspection and training date on Renewal Dates. Days left and the red, amber or green band fill in; Renewal Budget shows the cost by month.
Fill Scorecard History with one row for each month. Scorecard turns it into twelve measures with lights, trends and the money behind each gap; Targets shows your own best and worst month.
Open Monday Actions: the largest gaps become actions with an owner, a date and the money at stake. Print the first five for the Monday meeting.
Use the 18 tools: each answers one question with a verdict. Change the yellow inputs to try another source, technician, renewal item or target.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Leads and Scorecard Dashboard and the Charts every week. A one-person owner-operator with one van uses the same sheets; a shop with a dispatcher uses the dispatcher columns.

listing.title: HVAC and Plumbing Contractor Excel Template: Lead Sources, Reviews, Renewal Dates, Owner Scorecard, Monday Actions
listing.headline: Where work comes from and the one page you read on Monday
listing.description:
Know where your work comes from and what to fix this week, in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-run residential and light-commercial HVAC and plumbing shop with 1 to 15 technicians. A one-person owner-operator with one van uses the same sheets; a shop with a dispatcher uses the dispatcher columns.

Marketing Spend holds each source and month: spend, calls, booked jobs, sold jobs and revenue. Source Results ranks every source by revenue per spend with a keep, renegotiate or drop verdict, and the cost per booked job tool shows a source that is cheap per lead but costly per booked job. Reviews and Referrals keep counts only by technician and month, and the Review Request Gap Finder lists completed jobs with no request.

Renewal Dates tracks licence, insurance, registration, inspection and training dates with red under 30 days, amber under 60 and green later, and Renewal Budget shows the cost by month. The Owner Scorecard reads twelve measures from your own history, each green, amber or red against targets you set, with the trend, a one-line note and the money behind the gap. The weakest link tool and Monday Actions turn the largest gaps into actions with an owner and a date.

18 tools answer weekly questions with a clear verdict. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to customers, landlord accounts, technicians, your office, your equipment supplier, the accountant and the insurance agent.

This is part eight of the HVAC and Plumbing Contractor suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no per-technician fee: you keep your data. A demo copy full of sample data and a blank copy are included. Targets are yours to set; a typical range is a place to start, check your own numbers. It helps you keep track of your business and does not promise results.
